headline: July uprising crimes case: Verdict against ex-DMP commissioner and 4 others on Sunday
summary: The International Crimes Tribunal will deliver the judgment for five police officers, including a former Dhaka Metropolitan Police commissioner, this Sunday.
details: The International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) is set to deliver its verdict on Sunday regarding crimes committed during the July uprising.
The judgment will be delivered against five police officers, including a former commissioner of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP).
The proceedings have been scheduled for Sunday, and the verdict is expected to be a significant development in the legal process following the student-led uprising.
According to reports, the proceedings will be broadcast live on BTV, allowing the public to follow the legal outcome of the case.
caption:
A former DMP commissioner and four other police officers face their verdict this Sunday.

The International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) is set to deliver its verdict on Sunday regarding crimes committed during the July uprising.

The judgment will be delivered against five police officers, including a former commissioner of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP).

The proceedings have been scheduled for Sunday, and the verdict is expected to be a significant development in the legal process following the student-led uprising.

According to reports, the proceedings will be broadcast live on BTV, allowing the public to follow the legal outcome of the case.

headline_marked: 3 gold medals for Bangladesh in [[first Asia-Pacific AI Olympiad]]
headline: 3 gold medals for Bangladesh in first Asia-Pacific AI Olympiad
summary: Bangladesh secured the highest number of gold medals among all participating nations, competing against 18 countries including China, Russia, and Japan.
details: Bangladesh has won three gold medals at the first-ever online Asia-Pacific Artificial Intelligence Olympiad (APOAI). The country secured the highest number of gold medals among all participants, winning three out of the total ten gold medals awarded.

The gold medalists are Labib Shahriar from Homna Adarsha High School, Md. Saiduzzaman from Moulvibazar Government College, and Tridib Roy from Notre Dame College. They ranked 4th, 5th, and 9th respectively in the final global standings.

Four other students received honorable mentions: Naofil Rahman, Naira Nawar Ahmed, Ananya Zarif Akanda, and Mobtasim Chowdhury Priyam. Murtaza Abdullah was also a member of the eight-student Bangladeshi delegation.

The competition took place on June 13 via online video proctoring and screen recording. Participants had six hours to solve four machine learning problems across domains including astronomy, audio processing, wildlife images, and chemistry using the Borium platform.

The team was led by Professor Dr. B M Moinul Hossain, Director of the Institute of Information Technology (IIT) at Dhaka University, and coached by Associate Professor Md. Azam Khan of Daffodil International University.

The Bangladesh AI Olympiad activities began in April, followed by regional rounds in May and a national final at BUBT on May 16. The final team was selected after a national selection camp held from May 20 to 23.
caption:
Bangladesh dominates the first Asia-Pacific AI Olympiad, winning the most gold medals of any country!

Bangladesh has won three gold medals at the first-ever online Asia-Pacific Artificial Intelligence Olympiad (APOAI). The country secured the highest number of gold medals among all participants, winning three out of the total ten gold medals awarded.

The gold medalists are Labib Shahriar from Homna Adarsha High School, Md. Saiduzzaman from Moulvibazar Government College, and Tridib Roy from Notre Dame College. They ranked 4th, 5th, and 9th respectively in the final global standings.

Four other students received honorable mentions: Naofil Rahman, Naira Nawar Ahmed, Ananya Zarif Akanda, and Mobtasim Chowdhury Priyam. Murtaza Abdullah was also a member of the eight-student Bangladeshi delegation.

The competition took place on June 13 via online video proctoring and screen recording. Participants had six hours to solve four machine learning problems across domains including astronomy, audio processing, wildlife images, and chemistry using the Borium platform.

The team was led by Professor Dr. B M Moinul Hossain, Director of the Institute of Information Technology (IIT) at Dhaka University, and coached by Associate Professor Md. Azam Khan of Daffodil International University.

The Bangladesh AI Olympiad activities began in April, followed by regional rounds in May and a national final at BUBT on May 16. The final team was selected after a national selection camp held from May 20 to 23.
